_note: Starting content from the St Jude prototype. Facility staff must review every entry against local SOPs before relying on it.

severities.label: Stop now
severities.desc: Instrument or specimen may be at risk

resolution_types: Stopped on its own, cause unknown

problem_areas.label: Autoloader, cassette or grid transfer
hold: Pause the automated run. Do not repeat a failed load, dock or transfer command more than once.
Do not vent, open hatches, or touch the autoloader or dewars.
Leave the system in its current state. Staff will decide how to recover.
record: Exact error text and the time
Cassette position and grid slot involved
A photo or screenshot of the status screen

symptoms.label: Cassette will not dock or undock
Wrong or missing grid after load
Grid stuck or dropped during transfer

problem_areas.label: Vacuum, LN2 level or temperature alarm
hold: Stop acquisition. Leave the column valves and the screen as they are.
Do not clear alarms or restart the microscope computer or server.
Do not refill or change LN2 yourself unless you are trained and the SOP says to.
record: Gauge or value shown, if any
What was happening when it appeared

problem_areas.label: Beam, illumination or alignments
general: Confirm you are on the intended preset (magnification, spot size, C2 intensity) and nothing was changed after the last alignment.
Confirm the column valves are open and the screen is raised.
Compare with the facility daily-alignment record. Only redo alignments your training covers.
avoid: Do not adjust gun settings, the C2 aperture or the objective aperture unless you are trained and authorized.

symptoms.label: No beam or beam far off-center
steps: Confirm the column valves are open and the viewing screen is raised.
Check spot size, C2 intensity and magnification against your preset, and return to the preset if they changed.
Check that the beam is not blanked and that no aperture or beam stop is inserted, using the status indicators in the microscope interface.
If the beam is still missing, stop. Do not move apertures or gun settings.

symptoms.label: Beam not round, or it walks when intensity changes
steps: Look at the beam at your acquisition spot size and magnification. Is it elliptical, or does it shift as you change intensity?
Re-run condenser astigmatism and beam-shift pivot-point alignments only if your facility training covers them.
If values moved a lot from the last daily-alignment entry, note the numbers for staff.

symptoms.label: Suspected beam tilt or coma (asymmetric Thon rings)
steps: Acquire a short test exposure on thin ice or carbon at your usual dose and defocus.
Inspect the Fourier transform for asymmetric or elliptical Thon rings and run a quick CTF fit.
Compare with a reference exposure from the last staff-verified alignment, if one exists.
If the rings are asymmetric, ask staff to check coma-free alignment before collecting more.

symptoms.label: Dose rate unstable or different from expected
steps: Measure the dose rate over an empty hole. Note the value, spot size and C2 aperture in use.
Measure again after a few minutes. A steady offset points to a settings change. A continuing drift points to source or beam stability, which is a staff matter.
Change exposure time or dose rate in your protocol only after the value is stable.

problem_areas.label: Stage, eucentric height, focus or tilt tracking
general: Note the position, tilt angle and time when it started.
Compare the same behavior at a second position to separate a local problem from a global one.
avoid: Do not restart the stage controller or microscope server in the middle of a run.

symptoms.label: Image drift or smeared images after stage moves
steps: Wait for the stage to settle, then read the drift value in your software at the same position at two time points.
If drift falls with time, add a longer settling delay. If it stays high, move to a different grid square and compare.

High drift in only some squares points to the specimen or grid (for example buckling or an unsupported film). High drift everywhere points to the instrument, or to a recent thermal disturbance such as a cassette load.
If drift stays high everywhere, report the drift values and positions to staff.

symptoms.label: Eucentric height failure
steps: Note where it failed: the position, the magnification used for the routine, and the message or value shown.
Repeat the routine once on a flat, intact square, away from grid bars, broken squares and thick ice. Do not run it repeatedly.
Check that the routine has something with contrast to follow. An empty hole or featureless ice gives it nothing to track.
Check the result by tilting a few degrees the way your SOP does. A recognizable feature that stays in place means the height is right. One that walks sideways means it is off.

Run the routine on two or three neighboring squares and compare the heights. A large jump between neighbors points to an uneven or buckled grid or clip. A steady offset on every square points to the stage or its calibration, which is a staff matter.
On the cryo-FIB, confirm the stage is at the position your protocol uses before repeating the routine.
If the height sits at the limit of the stage range, or the routine fails on every grid, stop and call staff. Note the z values you saw.

symptoms.label: Autofocus failing
steps: Check that the autofocus target area is on ice or carbon, not on a grid bar or an empty hole.
Check the autofocus tolerance and defocus range in your protocol. Very tight tolerances can cause repeated retries.
Check that eucentric height was set at this position, since a wrong height often shows up as failing autofocus.
If the focus value sits at the limit of the lens range, stop and call staff.

symptoms.label: Tilt-series tracking lost (cryo-ET)
steps: Open the series and find the tilt angle where tracking failed.
Check that the tracking and focus area sits on the lamella or specimen, not on a gap, edge or grid bar, especially at high tilt.
Check that the pretilt setting matches the lamella or grid orientation as loaded.
If it fails at similar angles at different positions, increase the tracking exposure within your dose budget.
If the stage itself errors at high tilt, stop and call staff.

problem_areas.label: Detector, gain reference or frame saving
general: Check the camera status in the camera software: inserted or retracted, ready, and connected.
Acquire one short test exposure in a plain area to see whether it completes.
avoid: Do not restart the camera server or acquisition computer in the middle of a run without asking staff.
Do not delete or move existing frames.

symptoms.label: Camera not ready, not inserting or not acquiring
steps: Check the camera status in the camera software: inserted or retracted, ready, and connected.
Check that the acquisition software shows the camera as connected, and note the exact message.
Acquire one short test exposure in a plain area.
If the test fails, ask staff.

symptoms.label: Streaks, fixed-pattern noise or an old gain reference
steps: Note the date of the gain reference currently in use.
Acquire a no-specimen exposure and look for streaks, lines or fixed patterns.
Acquire a second exposure. A pattern that repeats points to the detector or reference. A pattern that changes points to the specimen or beam.
If the pattern repeats, ask staff whether a new gain reference is due.

symptoms.label: Frames not saving, missing files or disk errors
steps: Check free space on the acquisition drive and the destination storage.
Check that the destination folder is reachable: share mounted, permissions in place.
Check that frame format and number of fractions match your protocol and your processing plan.
Note the last micrograph that saved correctly and the time of the first failure.

problem_areas.label: Energy filter or slit
general: Confirm the slit is inserted at the width set in your protocol.

symptoms.label: Zero-loss peak drifting or off-center
steps: Confirm the slit is inserted at the width set in your protocol.
Re-center the zero-loss peak in an empty hole following the facility procedure and note the shift.
Check again after a while. A large repeated shift tells staff the filter is drifting.

symptoms.label: Low or uneven intensity with the slit in
steps: Compare intensity with the slit retracted at the same spot size and exposure.
Check that the slit is centered on the zero-loss peak and not offset.
If the image is uneven even when centered, ask staff to check filter tuning.

symptoms.label: Filter tuning fails
steps: Note the error message and which tuning step failed.
Do not repeat the tuning more than once. Ask staff.

problem_areas.label: Acquisition software (EPU, SerialEM, Tomo5)
general: Take a screenshot of the status or error and note the time.
Check the software log for the last error line and report it to staff.
avoid: Pause rather than stop where possible, so your position queue stays intact where the software allows.

symptoms.label: Acquisition stalls or is stuck on one step
steps: Take a screenshot of the status and note the time.
Check whether the camera, stage and microscope connections all show as responsive.
Compare with how long the same step took earlier in this session.
Pause rather than stop where possible.
Check the software log for the last error line and report it to staff.

symptoms.label: Hole or square finding fails (EPU)
steps: Check that atlas and square registration look correct on the map.
Check that hole size and spacing in the template match the grid in use.
Check ice-thickness or contrast filter thresholds. If they are too strict, most holes are rejected.
Test on a few holes manually before restarting the run.

symptoms.label: Script or Navigator error (SerialEM)
steps: Read the last lines in the SerialEM log window and note which script line failed.
Check that calibrations exist for the magnification, spot size and mode in use.
After a cassette re-dock or grid reload, check that Navigator items still register to the stage coordinates, and re-register if needed.
If the script worked earlier in this session, note what changed since then.

problem_areas.label: Ice, contamination or grid quality
general: Compare several squares across the grid before deciding it is a whole-grid problem.
Record grid slot and squares examined so staff and your lab can follow up.

symptoms.label: Ice too thick
steps: Compare ice thickness across squares using the atlas or square images and choose thinner squares.
If your software has an ice-thickness or contrast filter, apply it to select holes.
If the whole grid is thick, move to the next grid and note it for your next grid preparation.

symptoms.label: Crystalline ice or contamination
steps: Check whether the contamination is on one square, the whole grid, or all grids.
If it is grid-specific, choose clean squares or another grid.
If it appears on every grid and grows during the session, stop and tell staff. That can point to the instrument rather than the specimen.

symptoms.label: Few or no particles, or aggregation
steps: Look at a few holes in several squares to see whether distribution changes with ice thickness.
Acquire a handful of test micrographs and inspect them at full resolution.
If particles gather at hole edges or aggregate, treat it as a sample or grid-preparation issue. Screening another grid may be faster than adjusting acquisition.

symptoms.label: Beam-induced motion or charging
steps: Look at the motion traces of the first frames across several micrographs.
Compare holes at the center and edge of a square, and different squares.
If motion is high at the start of the exposure everywhere, ask staff about dose rate and exposure options.

symptoms.label: Broken squares or cracked grid
steps: Check the atlas for how many squares are intact.
Compare with another grid from the same batch if you have one.
If squares broke after loading, record the grid slot and tell staff in case it happened during transfer.

problem_areas.label: Data quality (CTF, motion, resolution)
general: Run motion correction and CTF estimation on the first 50 to 100 micrographs.
Plot CTF fit resolution, astigmatism, and measured defocus against your target defocus range.

Split the results three ways: by grid square, by acquisition time, and by hole position. A square-specific problem points to the specimen. A time-dependent one points to drift or ice build-up. A uniform problem points to the instrument or setup.
Share the plots and the pattern you found with staff.

symptoms.label: Defocus far from target
steps: Check the defocus range and autofocus settings in your protocol.
Check eucentric height at the acquisition positions.
Plot measured defocus along the hole-to-hole acquisition path to see where it departs from target.

problem_areas.label: Data transfer, storage or network
avoid: Do not delete, rename or move collected data until staff confirm it is safe.

symptoms.label: Disk almost full
steps: Check free space on the acquisition computer and on the storage target.
Estimate what the rest of the collection needs: movie size times micrographs still to come.
Tell staff the free space and the expected finish time so they can clear space or pause.

symptoms.label: Transfer stalled or share unreachable
steps: Check whether the transfer job or service is running and when it last moved files.
Check that the network share is reachable from the acquisition computer.
Leave source files in place until transfer is confirmed complete.

symptoms.label: Files missing or corrupted
steps: Note which micrographs or movies are affected and the time range.
Compare file sizes of good and bad files in the same folder.
Report the time of the first failure, since it helps staff correlate it with system events.

problem_areas.label: EMhub data transfer or data access
general: Write down your EMhub session or project name, the instrument, and the date of the collection.
Take a screenshot of what EMhub shows (missing session, wrong counts, error message) and note the time.
avoid: Do not rename or move session folders or files. The EMhub session record may refer to them by path.
Do not start the same transfer repeatedly. Wait for staff if the first attempt did not complete.

symptoms.label: Session or data not appearing in EMhub
steps: Confirm the collection has finished writing on the acquisition computer, or that the session is still running.
Check that the session is linked to the right project and instrument in EMhub.
Check that you are logged in with the account that owns the project.
Note the session name, the folder path where the data were written, and the time of the last file. Give these to staff.

symptoms.label: Transfer to EMhub-linked storage is stalled or slow
steps: Check whether the transfer job or service is running and when it last moved files.
Check free space at the destination storage and on the acquisition computer.
Check that the network share is reachable from the acquisition computer.
Leave the source files in place until the transfer is confirmed complete.

symptoms.label: File counts or sizes do not match
steps: Count the movies on the acquisition side and at the destination for the same session.
Compare file sizes of a few good and bad files in the same folder.
Note the time range of the missing or small files and report it to staff. It helps them correlate it with system events.

symptoms.label: Cannot open or download data from EMhub
steps: Check that you are logged in and that the project is listed under your account or lab.
Try a second browser or a private window to rule out a stale session.
Note the exact error text and the project name, and send both to staff.

problem_areas.label: EMhub booking or scheduling
general: Write down the instrument, date, time slot and booking name or ID involved.
Take a screenshot of the calendar or booking screen.
avoid: Do not create duplicate bookings to work around a problem. A duplicate can block the slot for other users.

symptoms.label: Cannot find or create a booking
steps: Check that you are logged in with your own account.
Check that the calendar is filtered to the right instrument and the right date range.
Check that your project or application is approved for that instrument. If you are unsure, ask staff.
Refresh the page, or try a second browser, then try once more.

symptoms.label: Booking conflict or overlapping sessions
steps: Compare your booking time with the neighboring bookings on the same instrument.
Note who holds the overlapping slot and the times involved.
Do not move or cancel anyone else's booking. Send the details to staff.

symptoms.label: Booking shows the wrong time, instrument or project
steps: Compare the booking with your confirmation or notes and note what differs.
Check the time zone and date display on the screen.
Do not edit the booking again until staff have seen it. Send a screenshot to staff.

symptoms.label: Cannot change or cancel a booking
steps: Check whether the booking is close to its start time, since some changes may be locked by facility rules.
Check that you are the owner of the booking.
Note the booking name or ID and what you tried, and send them to staff.

symptoms.label: Cannot log in or no instrument access
steps: Check that you are using the right account and address.
Check whether the problem is on one device only by trying a second device or browser.
Note the exact error text and send it to staff.

problem_areas.label: Cryo-FIB or lamella milling
general: Pause milling and do not start the next step until the problem is clear.
Save the current positions and record the milling step, current and pattern you were on.
avoid: Do not change beam currents or retract the stage while a lamella is at risk without asking staff.

symptoms.label: Lamella cracks or breaks
steps: Pause milling. Note the step (rough milling, fine milling, polishing) and angle when the damage appeared.
Image the lamella and surrounding area, and save the image with the position.
Check whether other lamellae on the grid show the same pattern. If so, the cause may be grid-wide (ice thickness, grid mounting) rather than the milling.
Tell staff before starting more lamellae with the same parameters.

symptoms.label: Charging, drift or unstable SEM or FIB imaging
steps: Check that the sample has the conductive layer your protocol calls for.
Compare image stability at lower voltage or current for imaging.
Check whether drift is on all grids or only this one.
If drift is at every position, ask staff to check shuttle and clip seating.

symptoms.label: Platinum or GIS coating problem
steps: Note which step failed: no deposit seen, or an issue with time or temperature.
Do not repeat the deposition more than once.
Image the surface to see whether any layer was deposited.
Ask staff to check the GIS before continuing.

symptoms.label: Lamella thickness not as expected
steps: Record your current thickness estimate and the method you used.
Check milling currents, pattern sizes and milling angle against your protocol.
Check for redeposition or ice contamination on the surface.
Change one parameter at a time and tell staff what you changed.

symptoms.label: Ice contamination on the lamella
steps: Note when the contamination appeared relative to milling and imaging.
Compare with another lamella on the same grid and with other grids from this session.
If contamination builds on every sample, ask staff to check the chamber and cold trap.

symptoms.label: Shuttle or transfer problem
steps: Stop. Do not repeat the transfer step.
Leave the shuttle and chamber in their current state.
Call staff now.

problem_areas.label: Something else or not sure
general: Write down what you saw, what you were doing, and the time.
Take a screenshot or photo of any message on screen.
If you are unsure whether it is safe to continue, pause and wait for staff.
